title: Buttery cabbage, walnut and goat's cheese toasts

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Every ingredient is a plain kitchen staple, from cabbage, apple and butter to goat's cheese, walnuts and bread, with nothing factory-made.

supermarket.reason: Soft goat's cheese, walnuts, white cabbage and wholemeal bread are all everyday lines at Tesco.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a frying pan, a grater and a toaster or grill, with simple frying and toasting.

works.reason: Half a cabbage fried in butter with apple and lemon, piled on eight slices of toast with 125g goat's cheese and 60g walnuts, makes a well-seasoned lunch for four.

honest_times.reason: Shredding half a cabbage, slicing garlic, grating an apple and toasting the walnuts and bread fit in about 15 minutes, and the 10-minute cook matches the 8 to 10 minute fry.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning appears in the steps, the names match their ids, and nothing unlisted is used.

seasonal_feel.reason: Buttery white cabbage with apple and walnuts suits a mid-September lunch, and the cabbage is the bulk of the topping.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear and in plain British English.

hearty_healthy.reason: Wholemeal toast piled with vegetables, cheese and nuts is a proper, appealing lunch.
